title: Span Sherpa — weekly handoff and ops notes
content:
Summary:
This is the weekly handoff for the Span Sherpa initiative (working name) — notes from the 11/21 standup + experiment status for tracing, dashboards, and cost telemetry. Intended for SREs on-call, tracing engineers, and the dashboard migration pair. Use this doc as the single source during the sprint gap week.

Attendees:
Aisha, Jonah, Lina, Marcus, Priya (came in for the last 20m)

Quick TL;DR:
- Adaptive span sampling experiment (windowed-probabilistic) currently reduces span volume by ~38% on mid-tier traffic in staging; latency correlation looks neutral.
- Dashboard migration: cross-cluster panel for span counts landed in PR 891; CSV import for legacy charts pending transform script.
- Cost telemetry: one customer (acct-redwood-731) showed a 12% spike in trace export egress on 11/19 — traced to excessive debug-level spans from onboarding flow.

What we ran this week:
1) Sampling experiments (staging):
   - Variant A: global fixed-rate 0.6 for low-cardinality services -> baseline reduction ~40%
   - Variant B: adaptive window (Span Sherpa alpha): computes p=clip(0.1 + 0.9*(1 - recentQPS/upperBound), 0.05, 0.95) per-service every 5m -> reduction ~38% but more stable across bursts
   - Logs: see OBS-1423 for the sampling rollout plan and metric definitions.
   - Observations: tail latency and p99 tokenization time unchanged; small increase in error span sampling on <1% of traces (likely due to window smoothing).

2) Dashboard work:
   - PR #891 adds a cross-cluster "span-volume by service" panel using the new metrics API.
   - Remaining: transform legacy query DSL into metrics API queries for the 8 most referenced dashboards; Lina owns transform script (ETA 11/24).

3) Cost telemetry and alerts:
   - Alert variant: new budget-aware alarm that fires when 3-day rolling span bytes > 1.2x projected budget. Marcus tuned thresholds after false positives on 11/12.
   - Incident: acct-redwood-731 debug spans — actioned by oncall to cut debug logging, opened OBS-1499 for follow-up.

Notes from the field / informal observations:
- Sampling smoothing window of 5m may be too long for services with aggressive autoscale; Jonah will test 60s and 2m windows next cycle.
- Prefix caching of span attributes reduced query CPU when reconstructing traces for dashboards; this is cheap win and should be part of deploy checklist.
- Some teams prefer deterministic sampling for compliance customers — we need an opt-in flag (see linked TODO).

Action items (owner — due):
- [ ] Lina: finish legacy dashboard transform script and run on staging (11/24)
- [ ] Jonah: run short window (60s) adaptive sampling sweep on canary service (auth-proxy) and report perf (11/23)
- [ ] Marcus: follow up with acct-redwood-731 PM to verify debug-log removal and check egress after change (11/22)
- [ ] Aisha: add opt-in deterministic sampling flag proposal in OBS-1423 (11/28)
- [ ] Priya: add a one-pager for runbook steps to handle span egress spikes (draft 11/25)

Open questions and risks:
- Is 5m window safe across global regions with different traffic rhythms? Risk: smoothing hides local spikes -> potential missed error capture.
- How to present sampling impacts to product teams without scaring them about "lost telemetry" — need clear metrics (sampled_error_rate, pre/post reconstruction coverage).
- Can we estimate cost savings per-customer if Span Sherpa is applied? We have rough figures but need a per-SKU model.

Runbook excerpts (quick reference):
- Spike in span bytes (alert): check top-10 services by span bytes (time range 1h), search for debug-level spans, open temporary debug-kill action, notify customer PMs.
- Sampling rollback: set global fixed-rate=1.0 and cancel adaptive controller (controller endpoint /api/v1/sampling/disable), escalate if error capture drops >5% on p95 errors.

Decisions made this week:
- Move forward with alpha adaptive window (default 5m) but enable shorter windows for selected canaries.
- Adopt prefix caching for dashboard reconstruction in staging as permanent optimization.

Hand-off notes to next oncall/sprint:
- If you see repeated false positives on budget alarm, check if transform script failed to map legacy metrics; Lina's transform logs live in staging: /var/log/obs/transform-lina-2028-11-21.log
- For any customer-facing incidents, ensure runbook step "notify-customer-pm" executed and link incident to OBS-1499.

Backlog / follow-up (short list):
- Implement deterministic sampling opt-in flag + compliance docs (Aisha)
- Per-customer cost model and simulation tool (Marcus + finance contact)
- Expand dashboard migration to the next 20 panels after transform script validated (team grooming 11/26)

Random notes to self (brain dump):
- Consider a "span heatmap" small widget that shows distribution of spans per trace length — could help explain sampling to product teams.
- Revisit the window formula: test variant with exponential decay rather than linear clip.

If anything urgent shows up overnight, ping #observability on Slack and assign to oncall with OBS-1423 prefix in the thread.

End of note.

Attachments: copied CLI experiment logs (staging) and PR link included in linked_artifacts above.
